Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

- rows 0–5, cols 18–24: four corners are 7 => output row 0 col 3 = 7
- rows 5–10, cols 0–6: four corners are 6 => output row 1 col 0 = 6
- rows 15–20, cols 6–12: four corners are 1 => output row 3 col 1 = 1
- rows 15–20, cols 18–24: four corners are 8 => output row 3 col 3 = 8

## Demonstration evidence
A demo had interior fill 8, grid lines 6, and a 27x23 input. Its output was 6x3:
`[[5,8,8],[8,8,8],[2,8,8],[8,8,8],[8,8,8],[8,8,5]]`.
Grid row lines at 1,4,7,10,13,16,19,22,25 and column lines at 1,8,15,22. Recolored cells matched four equal corners: marker 5 at rows 4&7, cols 1&8 -> first output row/col; marker 2 at rows 10&13, cols 1&8 -> third output row/col; marker 5 at rows 19&22, cols 15&22 -> last output row/col. This suggests output includes the rectangular subarray of compartments from the minimum to maximum special-marker lattice coordinates, cropping unmarked outer bands (here rows 1–4 and 22–25), while retaining fill color in cells inside that bounding extent.

## Useful solving procedure for recurrences
1. Identify the repeated lattice spacing, grid-line coordinates, and each compartment's interior fill color.
2. Interpret each potential output cell as a compartment between adjacent horizontal and vertical lattice lines; start with its interior fill.
3. If all four lattice corner values of a compartment are the same special (non-gridline) color, set that output cell to that color; otherwise leave its fill.
4. Determine whether the output is cropped to the compartment rectangle spanning the special-marker coordinates. The demo indicates it can crop marker-free outer bands; the solved test included the full 4x4 span because markers reached the extreme boundary lines.

Caution: First two attempted outputs were wrong; the third output above was confirmed correct. Do not confuse the dimensions of the compartment matrix with the number of exceptional markers. The first demo output was 6x3 despite the full lattice having additional unmarked outer bands."
